definition: The multiplicative weights update method is an algorithmic technique most commonly used for decision making and prediction, and also widely deployed in game theory and algorithm design.
details: The simplest use case is the problem of prediction from expert advice, in which a decision maker needs to iteratively decide on an expert whose advice to follow. The method assigns initial weights to the experts (usually identical initial weights), and updates these weights multiplicatively and iteratively according to the feedback of how well an expert performed: reducing it in case of poor performance, and increasing it otherwise. It was discovered repeatedly in very diverse fields such as machine learning (AdaBoost, Winnow, Hedge), optimization (solving linear programs), theoretical computer science (devising fast algorithm for LPs and SDPs), and game theory.

explainer.lead: The multiplicative weights update method is an algorithmic technique for decision making and prediction, widely used in game theory and algorithm design. It matters because a simple weight-update rule solves prediction and learning problems across many fields.

tiers.eli5: You listen to several advisers, give each a score, and after each round shrink the scores of those who were wrong and raise those who were right.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to prediction from expert advice, assigning initial weights and updating them multiplicatively according to each expert's feedback. A pitfall is that poorly performing experts are only down-weighted gradually, not removed, so bad advice still carries weight.
tiers.paperLevel: Initial weights, usually identical, are assigned to experts; after each round weights are updated multiplicatively, reduced for poor performance and increased otherwise. The method was discovered repeatedly across diverse fields.

explainer.example: In prediction from expert advice, a decision maker starts all experts at equal weight, then after each round lowers the weight of experts who predicted poorly.
